findings.title: Resistive seed unconditionally overrides caller-provided guess
findings.message: For every qualifying network, the resistive seed now unconditionally replaces whatever guess the caller passed in, including warm starts. The seed adds a network scan, a full linear solve and a 64-step bisection to every analog solve. Because `guess` is then non-empty, later branches that test `len(guess) == 0` (cold retries) see a different state than the caller provided. This silently changes solver behavior beyond the narrow cold-start failure it was meant to repair.
findings.suggestion: Keep the caller's guess for the first Newton attempt and use the resistive seed only as a bounded retry when that attempt fails. Alternatively, apply it only when `len(guess) == 0` or at discontinuities such as a pulse edge. Keep the original `len(guess)==0` information in a separate variable so the later fallback branches still see the caller's state.

findings.title: Possible index panic in parity test
findings.message: `Sources[0]` is indexed without checking the length. If the source list is empty, the test panics instead of failing with diagnostics.
